$comment: Extractor INPUT contract (WS-13 §3/§13). Hand-maintained and reviewed: a row's `risk` is what the extractor stamps onto the generated WinterProviderDescriptor, and promoting one to "approved" is a deliberate, reviewed edit. Lane X's scripts/provider-source-sync.ts is the consumer; the spine only establishes the file. No upstream source is vendored under this directory — see README.md.

reasons: gateway: capability parity is model-by-model (WS-13 §14.4); per-request provider/data-policy controls must be preserved
reasoning continuity is tool-loop fragile (WS-13 §8.2: missing reasoning state mid-loop is a hard error)
native cloud: deployment/api-version identity and Entra auth need their own proof (WS-13 §5)
native cloud: SigV4 signing + event-stream decoding need their own proof (WS-13 §5)
native cloud: project/location auth and partner-protocol differences need their own proof (WS-13 §5)

blocked.reason: Any upstream row whose transport is a browser session, a private/undocumented API, or a consumer subscription is blocked categorically and is never promotable by this file alone (WS-13 §5/§6).

notes: `codex-oauth` is NOT extracted from upstream — it is a Winter-owned provider carried over per D11 with originator "winter" (WS-01 §3), and its descriptor's `upstream.project` is "winter".
The twelve local OpenAI-compatible ids (WS-13 §12) are likewise Winter-owned: their inventories are machine-specific and always come from live discovery, so there is no upstream row to extract.
